beats.text: You keep telling yourself life is short.
Seneca — Roman statesman, Stoic — said you have it backwards.
Life is long enough. We just pour most of it away — on worry, on other people's opinions, on 'later.'
We guard our money and our land, then hand out the one thing we can never earn back: our time.
You live as if you'll never die. Then a whole decade is simply gone.
The fix isn't to rush. It's to stop giving your hours away.
Begin, now, to live. Treat each day as a whole life.
